items.title: How Anthropic secures its AI-native software development lifecycle | Claude by Anthropic
items.summary_1line: Anthropic Deputy CISO, Jason Clinton, details how the Security Engineering team secures a SDLC that has AI authoring 80% of merged code.
items.editor_note: Anthropic's Deputy CISO details how Security Engineering secures an SDLC where AI authors 80% of merged code.

editorial.tldr: Academic and industry work through early July proposed uncertainty-aware and multi-agent approaches to make AI-driven software development more reliable and controllable. By Jul 21, Anthropic detailed how it secures a real production pipeline where AI now authors 80% of merged code.
editorial.whats_new: Anthropic's Deputy CISO published how its Security Engineering team secures a software development lifecycle where AI now authors 80% of merged code — the thread's first concrete production account, following two earlier research/industry reliability proposals.
editorial.why_it_matters: If AI is going to author the majority of your codebase, Anthropic's own security controls for that shift are a closer reference point than academic reliability proposals — worth comparing against your own SDLC guardrails.
editorial.take_for_builders: If AI already authors a meaningful share of your merged code, compare your review and sandboxing controls against Anthropic's published account rather than relying on autocomplete-era code review practices.

beats.headline: Academic proposal targets uncertainty-aware multi-agent software development
beats.summary: UA-ChatDev proposes agents that flag their own uncertainty during collaborative coding, aiming to catch errors before they compound across roles.

beats.headline: Anthropic details how it secures an SDLC where AI authors 80% of merged code
beats.summary: Deputy CISO Jason Clinton describes the Security Engineering team's controls for a software lifecycle now majority-written by AI — the thread's first real production account.

open_questions: Do UA-ChatDev's uncertainty signals or similar techniques show up in any production AI coding pipeline, or do they stay academic?
Does Anthropic publish more detail on which specific controls — review gates, provenance tracking, sandboxing — catch problems in AI-authored code?
Do other companies at Anthropic's scale of AI-authored code publish comparable security accounts?
